findings: Owner request 2026-11-09: practice long questions for Chapter 8 in the same format as Chapter 1 (English and Roman Urdu), written from the chapter; not printed in the book. 24 questions numbered 1-24; by section: 8.1 2, 8.2 2, 8.3 2, 8.4 4, 8.5 6, 8.6 4, 8.7 4.

12 pairs (theory 5 marks + numerical 3 marks) covering polarization and its production, the three types of polarization, detection with polarizer and analyzer, Brewster's law (derivation), polarization by reflection, optical activity, Malus's law (derivation), polaroids and their applications, gravitational waves and their types, spacetime distortion, the interferometer, and Virgo/LIGO. Numericals use new values, recomputed in Python; any constant the chapter does not state as a number is given in the question. Book corrections followed: n1 sin(theta_p) = n2 cos(theta_p); reflected light polarized perpendicular to the plane of incidence; first GWs (2015) from merging black holes; GW amplitude is a unitless strain; 1 LY = 9.46 x 10^12 km.
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
